title: Select Ontology Lifecycle as a separate bounded-context candidate

artifact_type.representation_note: The decision carrier remains a bootstrap candidate. The recorded human selection resolves the planning branch but does not admit a bounded context or bind an unregistered owner role.

admissibility.ordering_limitation: The owner selected option 2 in conversation before the durable option IDs and prefilter receipt were materialized. The durable record maps that unambiguous selection to OLC-2-SEPARATE-BOUNDED-CONTEXT without broadening its scope.

selection.rationale: Ontology Lifecycle owns event history, replay, temporal cuts, projection, and lifecycle behavior that should not collapse into Governance ownership. Governance remains the upstream owner of authority, decision, admission, and invalidation semantics consumed by Ontology Lifecycle.

selected_context_model.name: Ontology Lifecycle
semantic_scope: Semantic event histories for ontology nodes and relations.
Temporal ontology cuts and deterministic replay.
Calculated projections and snapshots derived from canonical histories.
Lifecycle transitions, retirement behavior, and historical identity preservation.
Exact joins from governance events to semantic-event identity, digest, and cursor.
semantic_exclusions: Governance authority, decision rights, Constitution adoption, and admission policy.
Product capability adoption and product outcome ownership.
Storage-provider selection, deployment, publication, and external effects.

governance_boundary.dependency_semantics: Ontology Lifecycle consumes Governance-owned authority, decision, admission, challenge, and invalidation meanings without acquiring their ownership.

non_collapse_rules: Ontology Lifecycle bounded context is not the existing ontology-lifecycle directory.
Ontology Lifecycle bounded context is not its Project, Goal, Product Capability, runtime, DomainSpec source, system ontology, or implementation binding.
Governance context is not the Governance module, Governance Product, canonical authority store, or enforcement runtime.
A directional dependency does not transfer semantic ownership or authority.

resolved.resolution: Select a separate Ontology Lifecycle bounded-context candidate rather than classifying the current vertical as a Governance capability instance or leaving placement indefinitely unclassified.

remaining.condition: lab-architecture-owner, migration-owner, Governance context owner, and Ontology Lifecycle context owner are not yet bound in the admitted owner registry.
Bounded Context, CAV2 Context, Ubiquitous Language, Context Map, Capability Instance, Context Migration Manifest, and Context Lineage Record terms and artifact types are not admitted.
Governance has external candidate evidence but no Lab-owned admitted bounded-context artifact.
No Lab-owned Ontology Lifecycle context.json, language, contracts, context maps, or admission decision exists.
The exact DDD context-map integration pattern and owner contract between Ontology Lifecycle and Governance remain unselected.
No source-admission manifest, migration manifest, lineage postimage, relocation plan, or migration authorization exists.

decision_result.effect: Future context-migration planning will model Ontology Lifecycle and Governance as distinct bounded-context candidates connected by an explicit directional map.

excluded_effects: This decision does not admit either Ontology Lifecycle or Governance as a bounded context.
This decision does not create the contexts/ directory or move, rename, copy, delete, or rewrite ontology-lifecycle/.
This decision does not select the exact context-map relationship pattern or publish a cross-context contract.
This decision does not admit external CyberAlchemy-v2 source material or make source evidence Lab authority.
This decision does not admit definitions, artifact types, language, capability instances, DomainSpec sources, ontologies, runtimes, implementation bindings, or conformance.
This decision does not authorize Git commit, push, publication, release, deployment, external effect, or a stable-version claim.
successor_obligations: Bind accountable architecture, migration, Governance-context, and Ontology-Lifecycle-context owner identities without collapsing their scopes.
Complete CTX-00 by authoring and admitting the context migration terms and artifact-type contracts.
Author the Lab-owned Governance bounded-context candidate from exact admitted source selectors.
Author the Lab-owned Ontology Lifecycle bounded-context candidate with its own ubiquitous language, scope, exclusions, and capability-instance boundaries.
Select the exact directional context-map relationship pattern and contract between the two context candidates.
Prepare source-admission, lineage, migration, validation, and rollback artifacts before any physical relocation.
claim_ceiling: This decision resolves only the planning placement of Ontology Lifecycle as a separate bounded-context candidate downstream of Governance meaning. It does not bind the currently unregistered architecture-owner role, admit either context, select the exact context-map pattern, migrate bytes, authorize implementation, publish, deploy, or establish the first stable version.
